tasks.short: Locate and review geoscience research and reports

steps.what: Define the geological question, source scope and relevance criteria
Search article and report catalogues and remove duplicate references
Screen candidate abstracts and report descriptions for geological relevance

loop.purpose: Order candidate abstracts by the scientist's stated relevance criteria
loop.input: Actual catalogue titles, abstracts, source identifiers and scientist relevance labels
loop.output: Ranked source worklist with source text and explicit missing abstracts
loop.check: Scientist reads source text and labels relevance, checks known-relevant references and samples lower-ranked items for missed geological contexts
loop.stop: No automatic exclusion; stop only at the scientist's predeclared checked stopping rule, otherwise continue manual screening
loop.why_not_simpler: Keyword filters and deduplication are configured first; geological relevance in varied abstracts needs a bounded reading judgement

steps.what: Read original research articles and environmental, historical or technical reports
First record selected findings and exact source references for the research

tasks.design: Configure native search, saved queries and reference deduplication in the {OTHER} research-catalogue system. Only where screening remains cumbersome, use a bounded abstract-ranking worklist; the scientist decides relevance, reads originals and first records the actual findings in {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Catalogues contain repeated references and differently worded geological contexts.
tasks.enabler_now: Native reference tools and bounded relevance ranking can shorten navigation without substituting generated summaries for original sources.
tasks.still_hard: Historical reports may lack abstracts, and geological terminology varies by place and period.
tasks.human_edge: The scientist recognises relevant methods, locality and uncertainty that a ranked title may obscure.
tasks.altitude: Less search and screening navigation; interpretation and source selection remain scientific decisions.

reach.task: Review technical evidence for an environmental assessment
reach.learn: Relevance criteria and checks for missed local evidence

evidence.claim: ASReview LAB reorders abstracts while a person screens them; this supports relevance-worklist assistance, not a transferable time-saving percentage.

assumptions: Boundary includes actual search, review and research notes used in the scientific work. No new reading log, public summary or report send is added.

Catalogue publishers supply identifier, title, author, date and abstract where present. The scientist writes criteria and relevance labels in s1 and s3, retrieves missing descriptions manually and first records findings in s5. No fabricated source text or free metadata extraction is assumed.

Test native search and deduplication first. Nine of fifteen search hours are repeated query and duplicate handling; six remain for coverage checks. Six of twenty screening hours are repetitive worklist navigation and low-relevance triage that a checked ranked list can remove; fourteen remain for actual relevance decisions and coverage sampling.

Full-text reading retains all forty hours. The stopping rule is tested on known relevant records and lower-ranked material; a failed coverage check restores manual screening. Ordinary author saving within notes is retained and ungated.
unknowns: Coverage of abstracts for local historical reports
Whether native search already handles duplicates
Observed screening navigation and missed-source rate
research_questions: Does ranking reduce repeated navigation while preserving known relevant local and historical sources?

already_counted.description: Check search coverage, decide relevance and first capture source-linked findings

incremental.description: Audit missed sources and maintain queries and ranking inputs

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central: nine search and duplicate-handling hours plus six screening-navigation hours removed, less two upkeep hours, gives 13. Cautious case: historical reports lack useful abstracts, retaining all twenty screening hours; native query and duplicate handling still remove nine hours, less two upkeep, giving 7. Original reading and first research-note capture remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Communicate findings through papers, conferences and teaching

steps.what: Select findings and first record the argument, evidence and source pointers
Write research papers and explanatory text about geological findings

loop.purpose: Draft explanatory prose from the scientist's exact evidence brief
loop.input: Entered claims, results, limitations and source pointers
loop.output: Draft prose with each factual statement linked to an actual source
loop.check: Scientist compares every claim, number, causal wording and citation with the original result or source and corrects scientific meaning
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported claims or unavailable sources return to manual writing
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates supply section structure but cannot express new scientific reasoning; that reasoning is supplied and checked by the scientist

steps.what: Format existing figures, source lists and presentation or teaching materials
Check final scientific meaning, source accuracy and paper submission destination
outputs: checked communication materials and paper submission version

steps.what: Submit the checked research paper to the selected journal
inputs: checked communication materials and paper submission version

steps.what: Present geological findings and discuss them at conferences
inputs: checked communication materials and paper submission version

steps.what: Teach geological science and respond to university students' questions
inputs: checked communication materials and paper submission version

tasks.design: Configure native figure and citation templates in {DOCS}, then optionally draft explanatory prose from a scientist-entered evidence brief. The scientist checks scientific meaning and sources, submits the exact final paper through the {OTHER} journal-submission system, and still presents and teaches personally.
tasks.previous_blocker: Communication combines repeated formatting with new scientific argument and explanation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native references and templates plus a bounded source-grounded draft can reduce assembly and some prose work.
tasks.still_hard: A fluent explanation can misstate uncertainty or imply unsupported causation.
tasks.human_edge: The scientist defends findings, answers unexpected questions and chooses a scientifically honest explanation.
tasks.altitude: Less formatting and some prose drafting; scientific authorship, teaching and public explanation remain personal responsibilities.

reach.task: Explain environmental research to technical and public audiences

evidence.claim: Fixed evidence packs can support bounded explanatory drafts checked against originals; this is model knowledge, not a measured geoscience publication saving.

assumptions: Boundary includes the actual paper, conference participation and university teaching stated in the task. It adds no routine teaching log, attendance administration or extra public release.

Research results come from actual fieldwork and verified analysis; field first capture is explicit in 3703 and source review in 20390. The scientist first selects and records the communication claims and source pointers in s1. No free prewritten evidence brief is assumed.

Test native templates first. Seven of twenty prose hours are removed; thirteen remain for substantive editing and source checking. Four of ten formatting hours are repeated figure placement and reference layout; six remain for audience adaptation and checking.
All nineteen final-check hours, one actual paper-submission hour and thirty live communication hours remain. Ordinary author saves stay within writing and formatting, ungated and without saving.
The exact paper and journal destination exist before s4. Any change invalidates submission approval. The journal process is the OTHER submission-system category, not an autonomous publication action.
unknowns: Which figure and citation layouts already use templates
research_questions: Can every generated scientific claim be traced to the evidence brief without weakening limitations?

already_counted.description: Edit scientific prose, check formatted materials and verify final claims and citations

incremental.description: Audit draft errors and maintain source and formatting mappings

approvals.approved_version: Exact final paper, figures, sources and selected journal destination checked in s4; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central: seven prose hours and four formatting hours removed, less two upkeep hours, gives 9. Cautious case: a new interpretation needs all twenty prose hours because draft explanations distort uncertainty; four repeated formatting hours are still removed, less two upkeep, giving 2. Evidence selection, final checking, submission, conference exchange and teaching remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan and conduct geological fieldwork and testing

steps.what: Review the research objective, site evidence and sampling constraints
Write the geological survey, sampling or drilling and testing plan
Confirm practical site access, methods and crew responsibilities
Conduct geological surveys, collect samples and perform the planned field tests
First record sample identifiers, coordinates, observations and actual test readings
Check sample identity and field-record consistency against actual observations
Save the author's verified field data record

tasks.design: Use a native {DOCS} field-plan template for repeated method headings and sampling-table layout. Keep site judgement, crew discussion, all fieldwork and first capture in the {OTHER} field-data system; any existing automatic instrument transfer is already runtime and earns no new saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Field methods and site decisions vary, although the plan's structure can repeat.
tasks.enabler_now: Native plan templates can reuse layout without choosing sampling locations or methods.
tasks.still_hard: Access, geology, equipment behaviour and representativeness change in the field.
tasks.human_edge: The scientist recognises when conditions invalidate the planned sample or test.
tasks.altitude: Slightly less plan assembly; field decisions and scientific responsibility are unchanged.

reach.task: Collect and document geological samples consistently
reach.learn: Sample identity, coordinate provenance and field quality checks

evidence.claim: Native field-plan templates can reuse headings and table layout; this is model knowledge, not automated fieldwork or a measured time saving.

assumptions: Boundary includes planning, field collection and the actual data record used for scientific analysis. No extra visit report, routine crew log or contractor order is introduced.

The scientist produces sample identifier, date, location, coordinate reference, method, observation and test value during s4 and first enters them in s5. Instruments may provide readings, but absent metadata and manual readings are fully counted in the fifteen entry hours.

Test native plan templates first. Three of fifteen writing hours are repeated headings and table preparation; twelve remain for actual sampling design, method decisions and first site details. Crew discussion remains separate from record entry.

All fieldwork, first entry and verification remain fully retained. The one-hour ordinary author save has no gate and no saving. The saved dataset is an actual input to map and report preparation in 3705, not a second copy of those outputs.
research_questions: Can a plan template remove layout while keeping sampling design and site-specific decisions explicit?

already_counted.description: Write site-specific methods, first capture data and verify sample identity

incremental.description: Maintain field-plan table layout and method headings

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central: three plan-layout hours removed less 0.5 upkeep gives 2.5. Cautious case: an unfamiliar drilling or geophysical survey method needs all fifteen plan-writing hours and a reusable template is not maintained. Site review, crew discussion, fieldwork and all data capture retain their full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare geological maps, sections, charts and reports

steps.what: Read fieldwork and laboratory results and establish the map or report purpose
Verify coordinate references, units, sample identities and source dates
Set up source imports and repeatable coordinate and unit conversions
Interpret geological boundaries, cross-sections and uncertainty from the actual evidence
outputs: interpreted geological map and section content

steps.what: Prepare geological map, section and chart layouts with source and scale information
inputs: interpreted geological map and section content

steps.what: Write report implications and verify geological meaning and output metadata
Save the author's verified geological report and figures

tasks.design: Configure saved import and conversion settings, fixed metadata checks and map-layout templates in the {OTHER} geographic-information system. Keep manual repair of incompatible sources, geological interpretation and report writing; native calculation runtime and ordinary saving receive no labour credit.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated import settings and layout work sit beside source incompatibilities and scientific interpretation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native saved processing and layout templates can reuse verified settings while exposing metadata exceptions.
tasks.still_hard: A technically valid layer can still misrepresent geology or uncertainty.
tasks.human_edge: The scientist interprets sparse evidence and explains what the map cannot establish.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated setup and layout; geological interpretation and resource implications remain scientific decisions.

reach.task: Prepare geospatial outputs with reliable source metadata
reach.learn: Coordinate provenance, compatibility checks and uncertainty display

evidence.claim: Native geographic-information tools can reuse import settings, fixed metadata checks and layouts; this is model knowledge, not measured geological-map savings.

assumptions: Boundary is preparation of actual maps, sections, charts and reports, not field collection or an external release. Field first capture is explicit in 3703; laboratory staff already produce their actual sample results and receive no saving here.

Inputs require sample identifier, coordinates and reference system, date, measurement unit, value and source version. The scientist verifies these in s2; missing or incompatible metadata are manually resolved in retained s2 and s3 time. No clean layer feed is assumed.

Test native geographic-information configuration first. Three of fifteen metadata-check hours are repeated fixed checks; twelve remain for interpretation and missing metadata. Seven of twenty setup hours are repeated import and conversion configuration; thirteen remain for source repair and unusual transformations. Existing conversion calculation runtime earns no saving.

Six of fifteen layout hours are repeated scale, legend, source-label and chart placement; nine remain for checking visual meaning and individual output details. All twenty geological interpretation and nine report-writing and verification hours remain.
The one-hour ordinary author save is fully retained and ungated. No generated fault boundary, inferred sample value, automatic resource recommendation or report send is introduced.
unknowns: Layer compatibility and coordinate metadata coverage
research_questions: Do saved settings preserve reference systems, units and source versions through the final map and cross-section?

already_counted.description: Repair source incompatibilities, check layouts and verify report meaning and metadata

incremental.description: Maintain source mappings and test processing and output templates

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central: three fixed metadata-check hours, seven repeated setup hours and six layout hours removed, less two upkeep hours, gives 14. Cautious case: incompatible legacy layers retain all fifteen metadata-check and twenty setup hours; the output scale, legend and source-label template still removes six layout hours, less two upkeep, giving 4. Geological interpretation, report wording and author saving remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Fieldwork, scientific interpretation, teaching and source judgement remain central. Saved native settings and bounded prose assistance remove specific search, setup and formatting work.
reach: Geological technician: strengthen source and sample identity
Remote sensing scientist and technologist: preserve geospatial metadata in outputs
skills_to_grow: Research coverage and source-grounded drafting checks
Native processing templates and geological uncertainty communication
role.ambitious_version: A geoscientist who spends less effort rebuilding searches and outputs while retaining direct responsibility for evidence, interpretation and explanation.
